records.claim: how and from what the release was built, written and signed by the Sign job

what each Build, Rebuild, Check and Release step did and produced (apk, build, rapk, rebuild; scanners, acceptance, runtime: the scan, suite, FIPS and guide results for the exact candidate digests; release-verify to release-postverify: what Release verified, signed, published and attached), Build, Rebuild and Check records are made under a throwaway key and re-signed by Sign (stage-sign.yml) with the release key, signed with the KMS key and its Rekor entry is recorded beside each (release-verify's own record stays unsigned: it runs under the throwaway key), and Release's own records are signed with the KMS key and their Rekor entries are recorded; the next stage verifies each, and a customer can read Release's own as extra evidence

a signature on the public images in both registries and on the release files (SBOMs, lock files, dependency evidence, checksums and the release policy), each with a Rekor entry, and the dry run's forged material signed to prove it is refused

the release manifest (images by digest in both registries, the VEX files' hashes, the requirements baseline and the test evidence, the archives and apks as Build attested them) attached to each public image digest as an OCI referrer, signed with the KMS key; its Rekor entry is recorded; the GHCR referrer is required and the Docker Hub mirror is best-effort with a warning
the keyless signature of the automatic patch tag, checked by admission
